title.suggested: Barbershop talk cites Tom Allen's poor end as a warning to young fighters

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat's barbershop column quoted a man who said Tom Allen, once king of the ring, died at his Market Street place without $200 to his name, a lesson for young fighters.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Sunday Morning, September 6, 1903', page 5.

facts.fact: A speaker in a barbershop column said Allen spent his last days at his place on Market Street, 'lived on rum', and died without $200 to his name

notes: A semi-fictional conversation column; the claims are hearsay from unnamed speakers. Allen is a brief example in a long piece about local prize fighting, Corbett and Charlie Haughton. The current summary's 'left no estate' overstates it; the text says he did not leave $200.
